The opening frame shows the object already moving. Start the mechanism about 5 seconds in, at the clue scene. YouTube title seed: Why Does the Jet Bridge Keep Moving?
YouTube description seed: Next time you board, look for the little wheel by the door. Did you ever feel the bridge move? #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts
The central fact: The bridge follows the plane up and down, so its floor stays level with the door.
The later surprise: A little wheel touching the plane tells it when to move, and you can sometimes feel it.
The very first frame shows the end of a jet bridge at an airliner door, the bridge floor easing slightly upward while passengers step aboard. It is already moving in the first frame, and nothing in the first second gives the answer away.
What changes inside each 6s clip:
Scene 1 (contradiction, 0-6s): Opening: the bridge floor easing upward at the door as passengers board. About 2s in, a passenger's foot crosses the sill; about 4s in, the bridge eases again.
Scene 2 (clue, 6-12s): Mechanism starts about 5s in. Close on the real small wheel on its arm resting against the fuselage (real parts or physical props only, no animation or cutaway); about 2s in, the wheel turns slightly; about 4s in, the view widens to the bridge cab.
Scene 3 (mechanism, 12-18s): Outside view of the bridge and plane at the gate; about 2s in, bags go into the hold; about 4s in, the plane's door edge and the bridge floor stay level.
Scene 4 (second_reveal, 18-24s): A fuel truck at the wing; about 2s in, a passenger in the bridge pauses as the floor gives a tiny jolt; about 4s in, they glance down and smile.
Scene 5 (payoff, 24-30s): The last passenger walks into the plane; about 3s in, return to the exact opening: the same bridge end at the same door with the floor easing upward, same framing as scene 1's first frame, so it loops.
Fact boundaries: The auto-level requirement cited is a US standard for jet bridges; designs vary by manufacturer. Do not show the bridge hitting or damaging a plane. Keep brand names off generated equipment.

facts.statement: In the US, a jet bridge attached to a plane must have an automatic leveler that follows the plane up and down as it is loaded and unloaded, keeping the floor level with the door sill.
A small wheel on the bridge rests against the plane's body; as the plane rises or sinks, the wheel turns and the bridge moves to match.
Passengers, bags and fuel change the plane's weight at the gate, and that makes it slowly rise or settle; you can sometimes feel the bridge give a small jolt as it adjusts.
